findings.title: Embedded service manifest cannot load after blanket removal
findings.evidence: seed.groups retains module-relation-writers but accessBindings is removed. Unchanged internal/manifest/linkage.go:503-514 produces ErrGroupNeverGranted for that exact shape; manifest.Load returns joined faults. servicemanifest.Load is called by loadOwnManifest and cmd/kaname/serve.go:462-464 returns the error before registration bootstrap.
findings.fix: Provide a valid transition for the compatibility group without restoring a blanket grant or weakening general manifest validation; update actual embedded-manifest positive/negative probes.

findings.title: Upgrade cannot resolve legal legacy registrations with omitted parent claims
findings.evidence: Pre-1031 #982 allows a pointer registration with empty parent_project_id and parent_chain; the valid project pointer remains in relation_fact. New migration creates resource_registration_scope empty. The first-upgrade census joins only mirror parent_project_id or project parent_edge, never pointer facts or a canonical backfill; p[0]==empty is always rejected at line113 even with complete account/module assignments. SavedRegistrationScopeTx in registration_scope_reader.go:156-165 repeats the missing source and returns no scope for these legacy objects.
findings.fix: Resolve/backfill pre-existing canonical scopes from authoritative registration pointer data using the #982 rules, preserving claims. Cover first upgrade and cleanup/publication of a pre-1031 omitted-claims object; refuse truly unresolved scope.

findings.title: Named AW cases do not cover the accepted refusal and lifecycle transitions
findings.evidence: AW06:247-253 uses a direct vpc/project refusal instead of a child under a B container. AW07:255-257 has only the A success. AW13:438-447 has only allowed cleanup. AW14:279-286 denies an unknown object, not a registered B object, and never tests forbidden publication removal. AW19:346-367 uses repo Get/List only; no public normal Revoke/Delete and subsequent reseed/deletion persistence. AW22:391-396 toggles retirement without proving a standing cluster grant existed, was removed, and stayed removed, and has no rollback/reupgrade. These branches can regress while the named cases pass.
findings.fix: Complete these same accepted GWT pairs with existing real writers, a pre-1031 snapshot, normal binding lifecycle and negative access-state snapshots; establish fixture state before retirement. Do not replace required branches with unknown-object rejection or merely successful plan application.

findings.title: Successful no-op Down makes the next Up fail on existing tables
findings.evidence: Down executes SELECT 1 and preserves all three tables while the migration runner records the migration as rolled back. A subsequent Up executes unconditional CREATE TABLE for those existing names and fails. The data-preservation intention is valid but this is not a repeatable rollback/upgrade path.
findings.fix: Declare this migration explicitly irreversible by failing Down, or make the supported rollback/reapply procedure preserve both ledger contents and consistent migration bookkeeping. Keep binary-only rollback instructions explicit.

positive_static_observations: Identity and account authority separated, real roster reused, no cluster/admin fallback introduced in account model.
Register, Unregister, publish, emitAttempt enforce authority; missing dependency refuses; backend error uses canonical unavailable text.
Admission result reused for registration account check/audit/backfill; PB preference kept in derivation error path.
Bootstrap uses ordinary binding writer, subjects, emitted-set, relation outbox and audit in one tx; assignment ledger prevents old IDs from resurrection.
Owned revoke takes deactivation locks and removes exact emitted set; explicit operator retirement flag is present.
limitations: No source edits, builds, tests, lint, runtime, push, PR, CI or publication.
Findings are source-derived, not executed failures.
Approval of acceptance digest remains valid; this implementation is not approved.
